chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him).

In a case of a pledge (rahn) where the pledgor (rahin) and the pledgee (murta-hin) differed regarding it, the pledgor said: 'It is such and such,' and the pledgee said: 'It is more than that.' Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'The pledgee is believed until he covers the value, because he is its trustee.'

key_terms.يُصَدَّقُ: Is believed/verified (benefit of the doubt is given)

ai.seo_question: How is a dispute over the value of a pledged item resolved in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, the principle of *ta'shiq* (presumption of truth) is applied to the pledgee because he acts as a trustee (*amin*) holding the item for the debtor. This ruling prioritizes the holder's testimony regarding the item's condition or value, provided his claim is reasonable and sufficient to cover the debt, reflecting the fiduciary nature of the pledge contract in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the legal weight given to the party in possession when disputes arise over the collateral's state.
